name: Pelvic Girdle Pain and Sacroiliac-region Pain
summary: Pelvic girdle pain (PGP) is pain felt between the back of the pelvis (the area between the iliac crest and the gluteal fold, near the sacroiliac joint) and sometimes at the front, over the pubic symphysis. It may spread to the buttock or the back of the thigh.

looksLike: Pain at the back of the pelvis, one or both sides, sometimes with pubic symphysis pain.
Worse with walking, climbing stairs, turning in bed, standing on one leg, getting in and out of a car.
Often does not follow a nerve-root pattern and is usually felt below the L5 level.

book.title: Pelvic Girdle Pain and Sacroiliac-region Pain

blocks.text: **Pelvic girdle pain (PGP)** is pain felt between the back of the pelvis (the area between the iliac crest and the gluteal fold, near the sacroiliac joint) and sometimes at the front, over the pubic symphysis. It may spread to the buttock or the back of the thigh. It is common in pregnancy and after childbirth, but it also occurs in men and non-pregnant women [Ref - to verify].

The **sacroiliac joints (SIJ)** connect the sacrum to the pelvic bones. They move a small amount and rely on ligaments and muscles for stability. The exact cause of PGP is still debated. Joint, ligament, muscle, hormonal and load-handling factors may all contribute. There is no proven single mechanism.

blocks.text: Honest note: no single test proves the SIJ is the source of pain. Clusters have better value than single tests, and the best confirmation in research is diagnostic SIJ injection, which is not a physiotherapy test [Ref - to verify].
E1. Thigh thrust (posterior pelvic pain provocation, P4)

Supine, hip flexed to about 90 degrees, knee bent

A negative test does not exclude the SIJ. Groin pain suggests the hip
Applying force too quickly; allowing the pelvis to rotate; confusing groin or buttock muscle pain with SIJ pain
Use only gentle force; stop if painful or if the patient feels unwell

blocks.text: E3. Other provocation tests (known cluster)

The five tests that are most often grouped are: distraction (gapping), thigh thrust, Gaenslen's test, compression and sacral thrust [Ref - to verify]. The cluster is usually described as positive when at least 3 of the 5 reproduce the patient's familiar pain, and it is reported to be more useful than single tests. Interpret it with the history, because it does not prove joint disease.

rows: Supine; therapist crosses arms and presses outward and down on both anterior superior iliac spines
Familiar pain in the SIJ area
Supine at the edge of the bed; one leg hangs off, other hip held in flexion; gentle extension force on the hanging leg
Familiar pain in the SIJ area
Side-lying; downward force through the top of the iliac crest
Familiar pain in the SIJ area
Prone; downward force through the sacrum
Familiar pain in the SIJ area

blocks.text: In pregnancy, avoid prone and strong or sustained provocation tests; use the gentler positions and stop if the patient reports pain that lasts or other symptoms.
E4. Pubic symphysis palpation

Gentle palpation of the pubic symphysis, then resisted hip adduction with the legs in the crook position. Pain reproduction suggests symphysis involvement, and swelling or severe tenderness needs medical review.

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, leaking fluid, regular contractions in pregnancy
Placental problem, preterm labour, ectopic pregnancy
Severe headache with visual disturbance, sudden swelling, upper abdominal pain in pregnancy
Calf swelling, warmth, pain or sudden breathlessness
Fever with severe pelvic pain, cannot bear weight
Sudden severe pain after a fall or impact, or pain with weight-bearing in a runner or postpartum
Sacral or pubic ramus stress fracture
Saddle numbness, bladder or bowel change
Visible gap or severe locking at the pubic symphysis with inability to walk

blocks.text: **Defer:** forceful or sustained provocation tests and manipulation until red flags are excluded.

sections.title: H. Working diagnosis and decision pathway

items: Any emergency or urgent flag? **Yes:** act as in Section G.
Lumbar or hip source clearly responsible? **Yes:** use that pathway.
Posterior pelvic pain below L5, task-related pain, a positive provocation cluster or ASLR? **Yes:** working diagnosis is pelvic girdle pain (SIJ-region).
Pubic symphysis pain with tenderness? Working diagnosis includes symphysis involvement.
Persistent severe pain or no improvement with active care? Medical review.

rows: Gentle SIJ mobilization or muscle energy technique
May give short-term relief [Ref - to verify]
Positive provocation cluster, restricted comfort in a hip or pelvic movement
Supine or side-lying, low-grade oscillations or gentle isometric contractions
Soft-tissue work to gluteal and hip muscles

blocks.text: **Preferred starting choice:** education and a graded stabilisation and strengthening program. Manual therapy is optional for short-term relief. Do not claim to correct a pelvic misalignment or out-of-place bone; the evidence for that explanation is not credible [Ref - to verify]. Avoid high-velocity thrusts in pregnancy.

sections.title: J. Exercise prescription (example starting plan, not universal)

rows: Lying or sitting, gently draw the lower abdomen in without holding the breath
Lying with knees bent, lift hips
Lying on the side, knees bent, lift the upper knee
Hold a support, lift one foot
Standing with support, lift the leg sideways

blocks.text: **Pelvic belt:** a belt can give support during activity and may reduce pain for some patients [Ref - to verify]. It is a symptom aid, not a cure. Position it low, around the hips below the anterior superior iliac spines, snug but comfortable.

**Daily-life advice:** avoid wide leg positions, carrying loads on one side, long single-leg standing and stair climbing when avoidable; roll in bed with knees together; use a pillow between the knees; sit to dress.
**Symptom rule:** mild discomfort that settles within a short time is acceptable. Sharp pain, pain lasting after exercise, or any pregnancy warning sign means stop.

blocks.text: **Case:** A woman at 28 weeks of pregnancy has pain at the back of the pelvis on both sides. Pain is worse when climbing stairs and rolling in bed. No bleeding, no headache, no leg swelling. ASLR is painful on the right and eased when a belt is applied. Thigh thrust reproduces her familiar pain on the right. Neurological exam is normal.

**Working diagnosis:** pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain. **Plan:** education, a pelvic belt trial, avoidance of aggravating positions, gentle glute and trunk exercises, and review in 1 to 2 weeks, with a clear plan to refer for any warning sign.
**Questions and answers**

items: Why does relief with the belt matter? It suggests that the pelvis load transfer is part of the problem and that supportive measures may help. It does not prove which structure is the source.

Why not use forceful provocation tests in pregnancy? Because they can cause pain that lasts and the patient and baby deserve the lowest necessary risk. Gentle versions and a good history are usually enough.
Fever with severe sacroiliac pain and inability to bear weight. What do you do? Refer urgently the same day because infection is possible.
Why must hip pain be separated from SIJ pain? Groin and hip rotation pain lead to a different diagnosis and treatment pathway.
Why avoid saying the pelvis is out of place? The claim is not supported by good evidence, and it can create fear and unnecessary dependence on treatment.
**Initial approach:** education, activity advice, a belt trial and a graded exercise program.
**Justifying findings:** posterior pelvic pain, positive ASLR or provocation cluster, no red flags.
**Priority:** improving function and confidence.
**Manual therapy:** optional short-term adjunct, gentle.
**Exercise:** trunk, gluteal and single-leg control, progressing to functional tasks.
**Modalities:** limited role; pregnancy cautions apply.
**Tell the patient:** this is common and manageable; most improve; report bleeding, fever, calf swelling or severe pain.
**Avoid:** wide-leg and one-sided load positions, forceful testing in pregnancy.
**Measure:** pain, tasks, ASLR, stance control, questionnaire.
**If no improvement:** medical review.
**Referral triggers:** Section G.
**Discharge:** function restored and self-management plan in place.

blocks.text: **Assumptions:** no red flags, normal neurological exam, pregnancy beyond the first trimester.

items: **Can be tested:** whether exercise, belts or education reduce pain and disability; how well test clusters identify SIJ pain compared with injection.
**Hypotheses:** that poor load transfer contributes to pain; that belts reduce pain by increasing pelvic compression.
**Future questions:** best exercise type and dose; which patients develop long-lasting pain.

blocks.text: Evidence not graded until references are verified.

sections.A: Pelvic girdle pain kooleh ke peeche (sacroiliac joint ke paas) ya aage pubic haddi par dard hai. Hamal ke dauraan aur baad mein bohat aam hai.
sections.B: Pelvis ke peeche ek ya dono taraf dard, kabhi aage pubic haddi par. Chalne, seerhiyan charhne, bistar mein karwat lene aur ek taang par khade hone se barhta hai.
sections.C: Dard bilkul kahan hai aur kaun se kaam dukhate hain: chalna, seerhiyan, karwat ya kapre pehnna.
sections.D: Posture aur chaal, kamar aur hip ki jaanch aur neuro screen taa ke doosri wajahein rule out hon.
sections.E: Koi aik test SIJ ko dard ki wajah sabit nahi karta. Kai tests ka cluster zyada qeemti hai. ASLR aur thigh thrust ahem tests hain.
sections.F: Sciatica, kamar ka aam dard aur hip ke masle isi jaise lag sakte hain.
sections.G: Hamal mein khoon aana, pet ka shadeed dard, paani girna ya baqaida dard: foran doctor. Shadeed sar dard aur nazar ki tabdeeli bhi emergency hai.
sections.H: Red flags na hon, aur kamar ya hip saaf wajah na hon, to pelvis ke peeche ka dard aur positive tests: working diagnosis PGP.
sections.I: Halki SIJ mobilisation ya muscle energy technique, aur gluteal muscles par soft tissue kaam se thori der ka aaraam.
sections.J: Transversus abdominis, glute bridge, side-lying clam aur dheere dheere functional exercises.
sections.K: Garmi optional. Hamal mein TENS ehtiyat se, aur pelvis par ultrasound nahi.
sections.L: Pehli visit par red flags screen karein aur samjhayein ke PGP aam hai aur bachche ko nuqsan nahi deta. Phir amli salah, belt aur exercises.
sections.M: Dard, dard wale kaam, ASLR, ek taang par khade hona, chalna aur PGQ questionnaire.
sections.N: 28 hafte ki hamla khatoon ko seerhiyan aur karwat lene par dard hai. Khud socho, phir jawab dekho.
